Porn & Sex.name: James T.
Porn & Sex.body: 60 days today. The hardest part was never the urges — it was the shame keeping me isolated. Saying it out loud, even just here, took the power out of the secret.

Porn & Sex.name: Chris D.
Porn & Sex.body: Blocked what I needed to block and deleted the rest. Three weeks in and mornings finally feel like mine instead of something running me.

Porn & Sex.name: Morgan P.
Porn & Sex.body: Four months. My marriage is healing because I stopped lying to the person I love. If you're white-knuckling day one — it does get easier.

Porn & Sex.name: Andre W.
Porn & Sex.body: One week. I didn't realize how much of my day was spent either doing it, hiding it, or hating myself for it. That's a lot of hours back.

Porn & Sex.name: Neil R.
Porn & Sex.body: 200 days. The thing nobody warns you about: when the numbing stops, all the feelings you were numbing show up at once. Sit through that and you're most of the way home.

Porn & Sex.name: Sam O.
Porn & Sex.body: Day 3 and I want to quit quitting. Writing it down instead of acting on it. That's all I've got today and I'm counting it.

Porn & Sex.name: Tobias H.
Porn & Sex.body: 45 days. Told my wife the truth six weeks ago. She didn't understand and she didn't have to. I stayed honest anyway and that's the only reason we're still talking.

Porn & Sex.name: Victor L.
Porn & Sex.body: Three months. I stopped saying 'I relapsed' and started saying 'I chose it.' Sounds harsh. It's the first thing that ever gave me any power over it.

Porn & Sex.name: Damon K.
Porn & Sex.body: Two weeks. Turns out my trigger was never the phone. It was being alone at 11pm with nothing planned. Fixed the 11pm and half of it went away.

Porn & Sex.name: Eli B.
Porn & Sex.body: One year. I'm not cured and I don't think about it that way. I just don't build my life around hiding anymore.

Porn & Sex.name: Ross A.
Porn & Sex.body: Day 30. My husband said last night I've been actually present at dinner. He noticed before I did.

Porn & Sex.name: Gene M.
Porn & Sex.body: Day 5, and I nearly went back last night. Called my brother instead and talked about nothing for ten minutes. It passed. They always do, I just never waited before.

Alcohol.name: Dana R.
Alcohol.body: 45 days. Went to my best friend's wedding and didn't touch a drop. Danced all night with a clear head. Six months ago I'd have said that was impossible.

Alcohol.name: Tom H.
Alcohol.body: 200 days. My liver numbers are back in normal range — my doctor was thrilled. The physical healing is real, it just takes longer than you want.

Alcohol.name: Priya S.
Alcohol.body: Day 10. The insomnia is brutal but the fog is already lifting. One day at a time is the only way I can hold this.

Alcohol.name: Marcus D.
Alcohol.body: Three months. The 5pm craving still shows up like clockwork. It just doesn't get a vote anymore.

Alcohol.name: Helen F.
Alcohol.body: 30 days. I've saved almost $400 and I'm sleeping through the night. Nobody told me the sleep would come back.

Alcohol.name: Owen G.
Alcohol.body: One week. Told two people. That's the only thing I did differently this time, and it's the only time it's stuck past a weekend.

Alcohol.name: Rita C.
Alcohol.body: Five months. I was terrified I'd be boring sober. Turns out I was boring drunk and just couldn't tell.

Alcohol.name: Nate P.
Alcohol.body: Day 2. Shaky, angry, and here. That's the whole report.

Alcohol.name: Simone A.
Alcohol.body: Two months. The hardest part is other people's discomfort with my not drinking. I've stopped explaining myself and it got easier immediately.

Alcohol.name: Bill K.
Alcohol.body: Over a year. I still go to the bar with my friends. I just drive now, and I'm the one who remembers the night.

Alcohol.name: Charlotte E.
Alcohol.body: Three weeks. My kids stopped watching me at dinner to see how many I'd had. I didn't know they were counting.

Alcohol.name: Femi O.
Alcohol.body: Two weeks. Replaced the after-work beer with a walk. Felt stupid for about four days. Now it's the best part of my day.

Smoking.name: Ben O.
Smoking.body: 3 months without a cigarette. Climbed a flight of stairs yesterday without getting winded for the first time in years.

Smoking.name: Lena K.
Smoking.body: Two weeks. The cravings still hit hard after meals but they get shorter every time. Gum has been a lifesaver.

Smoking.name: Marcus J.
Smoking.body: One year smoke-free. Saved enough to take my kids on a real vacation. Every craving I said no to added up to this.

Smoking.name: Ivan S.
Smoking.body: Day 3, the worst one. Somebody told me the physical part is basically done by day 4. Holding onto that.

Smoking.name: Grace T.
Smoking.body: One month. My clothes don't smell. My car doesn't smell. I hadn't noticed it in twenty years and now I can't unsmell it on other people.

Smoking.name: Hugh D.
Smoking.body: Two months. I quit six times before. The difference this time is I stopped treating a slip as the end of the attempt.

Smoking.name: Paula N.
Smoking.body: One week. I'm irritable and everybody in this house is being very patient with me. Apologies issued in advance.

Smoking.name: Ken A.
Smoking.body: Six months. My resting heart rate dropped 12 beats. That's not motivation talk, that's my watch.

Smoking.name: Rosa V.
Smoking.body: Three weeks. The hardest one is the first cigarette of the day, not the tenth. Nobody warned me about that.

Smoking.name: Dermot L.
Smoking.body: 45 days. Vaping was supposed to be the way out and it just moved the problem. Off both now.

Smoking.name: Anya P.
Smoking.body: Day 10. Standing outside in the rain at 2am last week is what finally did it for me. What a thing to have done for twenty years.

Smoking.name: Terry W.
Smoking.body: Four months. My daughter asked me to quit for eight years. I did it the week after my grandson was born. Wish I'd listened sooner.

Substances.name: Ryan M.
Substances.body: 30 days clean. The first two weeks I couldn't tell if I was going to make it hour to hour. Now I can see a week ahead.

Substances.name: Alicia B.
Substances.body: Three months. Got a sponsor, go to meetings, use this app between them. Needed all three, not one.

Substances.name: Jonah F.
Substances.body: One week. Detoxed with medical help and I'd tell anyone reading this to do the same. Don't do it alone.

Substances.name: Camille R.
Substances.body: Six months. I have a job again. I have my sister's phone number again. Both took time and neither came back on day one.

Substances.name: Dev S.
Substances.body: Day 3 and everything hurts. Told the group at the meeting tonight. That's all I did today and it's enough.

Substances.name: Nora H.
Substances.body: One year. The urge doesn't fully go away, it just stops being the loudest thing in the room.

Substances.name: Titus J.
Substances.body: 45 days. Had to change my phone number and my whole Friday night. It's lonelier and I'm alive.

Substances.name: Maya D.
Substances.body: Two weeks. My mother cried when I called sober. I've got a lot of ground to make up and I'm not rushing it.

Substances.name: Errol P.
Substances.body: Two months. PAWS is real — the mood crashes around week 6 nearly took me out. It lifted. Ride it out.

Substances.name: Bea L.
Substances.body: Three weeks. Structure is the whole thing for me. Empty afternoons are where I lose.

Substances.name: Zack N.
Substances.body: Nine months. I relapsed at day 40 and came back at day 41. Everything I have now is on the other side of that decision.

Substances.name: Imani C.
Substances.body: Day 10. Eating three meals and sleeping at night for the first time in two years. Small stuff that isn't small.

Gambling.name: Derek W.
Gambling.body: Two months. Self-excluded from every site and handed the cards to my wife. Losing the access is what let me start.

Gambling.name: Sonia G.
Gambling.body: Three weeks. The urge always comes with a story about winning it back. The story is the addiction talking.

Gambling.name: Ahmed R.
Gambling.body: Six months. I'm paying it down $200 at a time. Slow, boring, and it's the first time the number's gone the right direction.

Gambling.name: Kelly T.
Gambling.body: One week. Deleted the apps, then deleted the browser bookmarks, then blocked the sites. Took three rounds to actually cut it off.

Gambling.name: Pete N.
Gambling.body: Three months. Told my brother the real number last month. Hardest conversation of my life and I slept afterward.

Gambling.name: Vera S.
Gambling.body: 30 days. It was never about money for me. It was about the 20 seconds before the result.

Gambling.name: Lou B.
Gambling.body: Day 3. Checked the odds out of habit twice today and closed it both times. Counting that as a win.

Gambling.name: Nathan K.
Gambling.body: A year. I still can't watch a game with the app on my phone. I know myself now, and that's not weakness.

Gambling.name: Tara M.
Gambling.body: 45 days. The lying was worse than the losing. I don't have anything to hide today and I feel ten pounds lighter.

Gambling.name: Callum D.
Gambling.body: Two weeks. My paycheck is still in my account on a Wednesday. That hasn't happened in three years.

Gambling.name: Rhonda F.
Gambling.body: Four months. Got a debt advisor through a free service. Should have called them five years and forty thousand ago.

Gambling.name: Sean H.
Gambling.body: Day 10. Boredom is the trigger, not stress. Once I worked that out I started filling the evenings instead of fighting the urge.

Social media.name: Jordan A.
Social media.body: 3 weeks off Instagram. My anxiety about how I look and what people think has dropped so much. Didn't expect that.

Social media.name: Wei L.
Social media.body: 45 days. Started reading books again for the first time since college. Turns out I had a lot more free time than I thought.

Social media.name: Mel C.
Social media.body: One week. Reached for my phone maybe 200 times out of pure habit. The hand knows before the brain does.

Social media.name: Ade O.
Social media.body: Three months. I stopped knowing everyone's opinion about everything and I am significantly happier.

Social media.name: Rosie B.
Social media.body: One month. Moved the apps off my home screen first, then off the phone. The two-step made it stick.

Social media.name: Kwame S.
Social media.body: Two weeks. Screen time went from 6 hours to under 2. Six hours. Every day. For years.

Social media.name: Tess V.
Social media.body: Day 3 and bored out of my mind, which I now realize was the whole point of the scrolling.

Social media.name: Milo H.
Social media.body: Two months. The comparison was the poison, not the time. I forgot I was measuring myself against people's best 30 seconds.

Social media.name: Farah Y.
Social media.body: Six months. Kept messaging, cut the feeds. That compromise is what made it survivable for me.

Social media.name: Iris N.
Social media.body: Day 10. My phone stays in the kitchen at night now. I fall asleep in about ten minutes instead of ninety.

Social media.name: Gus R.
Social media.body: Four months. Nobody noticed I was gone, which stung for a day and then set me completely free.

Social media.name: Priya K.
Social media.body: Day 5. Put a rubber band round my phone so I have to think before I open it. Ridiculous and it works.

Gaming.name: Alex P.
Gaming.body: 30 days without logging in. Didn't realize how many hours I was losing until I actually had them back. Started exercising again.

Gaming.name: Tyler B.
Gaming.body: 100 days. Grades are up and I'm seeing friends in person instead of just voice chat. No regrets uninstalling.

Gaming.name: Sam K.
Gaming.body: Day 10, and honestly the boredom is the hardest part. Trying to fill it with anything else instead of caving.

Gaming.name: Renee D.
Gaming.body: Two months. It was never about the game. It was about being good at something when nothing else was going well.

Gaming.name: Ivan T.
Gaming.body: One week. Sold the setup. Drastic, and I know myself well enough to know I needed drastic.

Gaming.name: Hana M.
Gaming.body: Six months. I still game — two hours on a Saturday, timer on. Some people can do that. It took me a year to find out I could.

Gaming.name: Bruno L.
Gaming.body: Three weeks. Was doing 6 hours a night and calling it relaxing. I was more tired after than before.

Gaming.name: Ollie J.
Gaming.body: 45 days. The friends in the guild were real friends and losing them was a real loss. Nobody talks about that part.

Gaming.name: Chidi A.
Gaming.body: Day 3. Deleted the account rather than deactivating so I can't crawl back at 2am.

Gaming.name: Lena W.
Gaming.body: A year. Finished my degree in the hours I got back. Same hours, different life.

Gaming.name: Marc S.
Gaming.body: Two weeks. Turns out I was avoiding one specific thing at work. Handled the thing and the pull halved.

Gaming.name: Kai R.
Gaming.body: Three months. My partner said he'd stopped trying to talk to me in the evenings. That sentence is why I stopped.

Food / Binging.name: Taylor R.
Food / Binging.body: Day 3 and honestly terrified I'll cave the second I feel stressed. Every hour feels like a mountain. But I'm not quitting.

Food / Binging.name: Monica G.
Food / Binging.body: 2 months. Learning to actually feel my emotions instead of eating them. Therapy plus this app has made a real difference.

Food / Binging.name: Diego F.
Food / Binging.body: Two weeks. Stopped weighing myself every day — it was making everything worse. Focusing on how I feel instead of a number.

Food / Binging.name: Ann-Marie P.
Food / Binging.body: One month. I eat at set times now whether I feel like it or not. Structure did more than willpower ever did.

Food / Binging.name: Josh V.
Food / Binging.body: Three months. The binge was never about hunger. It was about being alone where nobody could see.

Food / Binging.name: Lucia B.
Food / Binging.body: One week. Got the trigger foods out of the house. Not forever, just for now, while I'm building something.

Food / Binging.name: Ed T.
Food / Binging.body: Six months. I've had bad days. The difference is a bad day is now one meal, not the whole week written off.

Food / Binging.name: Femi A.
Food / Binging.body: Three weeks. Started eating breakfast. Sounds absurd but skipping it is what set up every 9pm binge.

Food / Binging.name: Hattie C.
Food / Binging.body: 45 days. The shame after was always worse than the eating and it drove the next one. Cutting the shame cut the cycle.

Food / Binging.name: Ravi N.
Food / Binging.body: Day 10. Ten minutes and a glass of water before I decide. Most of the time the urge doesn't survive ten minutes.

Food / Binging.name: Sylvie M.
Food / Binging.body: Four months. Threw out the 'good food / bad food' language. Food isn't a moral test and I'm not a bad person at 9pm.

Food / Binging.name: Owen R.
Food / Binging.body: Day 5. Told my partner what's actually going on after fifteen years of hiding it. She just hugged me.

Shopping / Spending.name: Nina R.
Shopping / Spending.body: One month. Unsubscribed from every marketing email. I didn't have willpower, I had a phone designed to break it.

Shopping / Spending.name: Carl B.
Shopping / Spending.body: Three months. $2,300 not spent. The rush lasted about a minute and the bill lasted a year.

Shopping / Spending.name: Aisha M.
Shopping / Spending.body: One week. Took the saved cards off every site. Having to type the numbers in stops me about half the time.

Shopping / Spending.name: Doug F.
Shopping / Spending.body: Two months. It was mood management. I only ever bought things after a bad day at work.

Shopping / Spending.name: Elle T.
Shopping / Spending.body: Two weeks. The 30-minute rule. Ninety percent of the time I don't want it thirty minutes later.

Shopping / Spending.name: Sanjay P.
Shopping / Spending.body: Six months. Cancelled eleven subscriptions I forgot I had. Eleven.

Shopping / Spending.name: Mo K.
Shopping / Spending.body: Day 3, and there's a package coming that I ordered before I started. Going to open it and not pretend it didn't happen.

Shopping / Spending.name: Grace H.
Shopping / Spending.body: 45 days. The parcels arriving was the actual high. Not the things. I have a closet full of proof.

Shopping / Spending.name: Tomás D.
Shopping / Spending.body: Three weeks. Started a list instead of a cart. Most things never make it off the list.

Shopping / Spending.name: Jill A.
Shopping / Spending.body: Four months. Told my husband the real credit card number. Worst hour, best decision.

Shopping / Spending.name: Ren S.
Shopping / Spending.body: Day 10. Deleted the apps and kept the browser blocked. Both, or it just moves.

Shopping / Spending.name: Victor E.
Shopping / Spending.body: A year. I have savings for the first time at 44. It wasn't income that changed.

Work.name: Priya N.
Work.body: Six weeks of eating lunch away from my desk every single day. Sounds small, it's the first boundary I've held in years.

Work.name: Ahmed K.
Work.body: 45 days without checking email after dinner. My kids noticed before I did that I was actually present again.

Work.name: Liz M.
Work.body: Day 10 of not opening my laptop on Saturday or Sunday. It felt wrong at first, like I was falling behind. I wasn't.

Work.name: Gareth O.
Work.body: Three months. Nobody at work has said a word about me leaving at 5:30. All that fear was mine.

Work.name: Noor S.
Work.body: One month. I was using work to avoid my marriage. That was very uncomfortable to write down.

Work.name: Dan V.
Work.body: One week with a hard stop at 6pm. Broke it twice. Kept it five times, which is five more than last week.

Work.name: Ines B.
Work.body: Six months. The company did not collapse. My health had been about to.

Work.name: Rob T.
Work.body: Three weeks. Turned off notifications on my phone entirely. The first Saturday was withdrawal, plainly.

Work.name: Chen W.
Work.body: Two months. Being busy was how I avoided being still. Still is where all the difficult thoughts live.

Work.name: Marta L.
Work.body: Four months. Took my first real holiday in six years and didn't check in once. Nothing was on fire when I got back.

Work.name: Sol A.
Work.body: Day 3 of a real lunch break. Sitting still for 30 minutes is much harder than it should be.

Work.name: Femi B.
Work.body: A year of protected weekends. My son asked why I'm around more. That question is going to stay with me.

Other.name: Jamie R.
Other.body: 21 days of choosing the harder right thing over the easier wrong thing. Whatever you're working on, it's worth it.

Other.name: Casey V.
Other.body: 3 months steady. Recovery doesn't fit one neat label some days — it's just choosing better, one hour at a time.

Other.name: Robin T.
Other.body: Day 5. New to this and still figuring out what my triggers even are. Glad this space exists for people who don't fit a category.

Other.name: Dev A.
Other.body: One month. Mine doesn't have a name that anyone would recognize. It still ran my life and it's still worth stopping.

Other.name: Nadia P.
Other.body: Two months. The mechanics are the same whatever the thing is — trigger, urge, act, crash, shame, repeat. Break it anywhere.

Other.name: Tom C.
Other.body: One week. Wrote down what I actually do and when. Seeing it on paper was worse and better than I expected.

Other.name: Erin K.
Other.body: Six months. Nobody's throwing me a party because nobody knew. I know. That turned out to be enough.

Other.name: Sam H.
Other.body: Two weeks. Told one person. That's the single thing that changed the odds for me.

Other.name: Wole M.
Other.body: 45 days. Structure, sleep, and one honest conversation a week. That's my whole program and it's holding.

Other.name: Bea T.
Other.body: Day 3 and white-knuckling. Still here at 9pm, which is later than I got last time.

Other.name: Callum J.
Other.body: Four months. Slipped at day 60. Came back at day 61 and stopped counting the slip as the story.

Other.name: Ruth E.
Other.body: A year. Not fixed. Just no longer organized around it.

Supporting Someone.name: Denise W.
Supporting Someone.body: For nine years I thought he stopped wanting me because of my body. Found out last spring it was porn. Not sure which hurts worse, but at least now I know it was never me.

Supporting Someone.name: Angela M.
Supporting Someone.body: Everybody asks how he's doing. Nobody has asked how I'm doing in three years. Finally told my sister the whole thing last week and cried for an hour. First real breath I've taken.

Supporting Someone.name: Rob F.
Supporting Someone.body: I held it together for everyone until the night I put my fist through a door. Then suddenly I was the problem. Learning here that the explosion wasn't the start of it — it was the end of ten years of nobody listening.

Supporting Someone.name: Priscilla T.
Supporting Someone.body: Stopped calling her boss with excuses. Hardest thing I've ever done, felt like betrayal. It wasn't. I'm not the reason she keeps her job anymore and I sleep better.

Supporting Someone.name: Marisol C.
Supporting Someone.body: One week of looking at my own life instead of managing his. I don't know what I like anymore. Starting there.

Supporting Someone.name: Kevin D.
Supporting Someone.body: 45 days. I'm a man whose wife is the one struggling and there is almost nothing written for me anywhere. This helps.

Supporting Someone.name: Terri B.
Supporting Someone.body: Three weeks. I can read their mood from the sound of the car door. I want to un-learn that skill.

Supporting Someone.name: Yvonne A.
Supporting Someone.body: Four months. Found a free Al-Anon meeting online. Sat with my camera off for the first three and just listened. It was the first room where nobody told me to be more patient.

Supporting Someone.name: Hannah L.
Supporting Someone.body: Day 10. He got sober and I thought that would fix it. Nobody warned me I'd still be carrying everything from the years before.

Supporting Someone.name: Dolores P.
Supporting Someone.body: Six months. I stopped waiting for the version of him I met. That grief was heavier than the leaving would have been.

Supporting Someone.name: Nia S.
Supporting Someone.body: Day 3 of writing things down with dates instead of arguing about what happened. I'd forgotten I was allowed to trust my own memory.

Supporting Someone.name: Frank R.
Supporting Someone.body: A year. She's still using and I'm still here and I've got my own doctor, my own friends and my own Saturday back. Both those things are true at once.

Anger & Control.name: Ray M.
Anger & Control.body: Took me 40 years to say the real word instead of 'I've got a temper.' My daughter used to read my face from the driveway. That's the part I can't unsee.

Anger & Control.name: Curtis B.
Anger & Control.body: The six rule is the only thing that's ever worked for me. I say the sentence, I walk, I come back in twenty. My wife said last week it's the first time in years she's finished a sentence.

Anger & Control.name: Hector V.
Anger & Control.body: Realized I hold it together all day at work and only lose it at home. That was a bad thing to find out about myself and it's the reason I finally started doing something.

Anger & Control.name: Doug S.
Anger & Control.body: Road rage was the one I thought was harmless. Leaving ten minutes early has done more for me than ten years of telling myself to calm down.

Anger & Control.name: Lamar J.
Anger & Control.body: One week. Found out my anger is never the first feeling. Underneath it every time is 'you don't respect me.' Every single time.

Anger & Control.name: Warren T.
Anger & Control.body: Two months. Started with sleep, of all things. Seven hours instead of five and half my fuse came back.

Anger & Control.name: Nico P.
Anger & Control.body: 30 days. My son flinched when I raised my hand to scratch my head. I'll be working on that memory for the rest of my life.

Anger & Control.name: Ade F.
Anger & Control.body: Six months. Signed up to a program through the county. Walking into that first session was the hardest door I've ever opened, and it's the only thing that actually moved the needle.

Anger & Control.name: Glenn R.
Anger & Control.body: Day 3. Left the room twice today instead of saying the thing. Came back both times. That's all I've got and I'm counting it.

Anger & Control.name: Marcus H.
Anger & Control.body: Four months. Learned the difference between apologizing and asking to be let off. Been doing the second one for twenty years.

Anger & Control.name: Ty W.
Anger & Control.body: Two weeks. Stopped rehearsing arguments in the truck. That was three hours a day of getting angry at people who weren't there.

Anger & Control.name: Bernard O.
Anger & Control.body: A year. She still watches me sometimes. That's not her being unfair — that's a lot of evidence on one side and not much on the other yet. My job is to keep adding to my side.
